conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode. Helpers: range(n) = high[n]-low[n]; body(n) = close[n]-open[n]; tailFraction(n) = (range(n)-abs(body(n)))/range(n); avgRange(N) = average of range over the N bars ending at bar 1; tick = instrument minimum price move (structural constant); highest(x,N)[k] / lowest(x,N)[k] = extreme over N bars ending at bar k; average(x,N)[k] = mean over N bars ending at bar k; ema = XAverage(close, emaLength); atr(n) = AvgTrueRange(n); swingHigh(k)/swingLow(k) = k-th most recent confirmed pivot (per T15's convention). Skipped the Contents and Acknowledgments pages per instructions (the Acknowledgments page, p11, is also one of the pages that lost inter-word spacing in extraction).

candidates.description: After a low-4 short signal (PullbackLegCounter.legCount==4, short side) triggers and then fails (price closes back above the signal bar's high), block further short pullback entries until a new bear trend-line break confirms bears regained control.
candidates.pseudocode: low4Triggered at bar k; close[j] > high[k] for some j>k (failure); block short entries until BearTrendLineBreak occurs

complexity.reason: chains the leg counter, a failure test, and a trend-line break -- each already its own design decision

candidates.name: TrailingStopBelowHigherLow
candidates.quote: if they are long in a bull trend, every time the market moves to a new high, they might raise the protective stop to just below the most recent higher low.
candidates.description: Exit: trail the protective stop to just below the most recent confirmed higher swing low each time price makes a new high.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && close[0] < swingLow(1) - stopTicks * tick
candidates.book_order_type: protective stop moved to one tick below the most recent higher swing low

complexity.reason: needs confirmed swing-low tracking plus a position-state read

notes: StopBelowRecentSwingLow (chapter 15) is the same mechanism, kept there without this glossary source citation.

candidates.name: MoveStopToBreakevenOnTest
candidates.quote: breakout test A breakout pullback that comes close to the original entry price to test a breakeven stop. It may overshoot it or undershoot it by a few ticks.
candidates.description: Once in a profitable position, if price pulls back to within a tolerance of the entry price, move the stop to breakeven.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() > 0 && close[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice() + toleranceTicks * tick
candidates.book_order_type: protective stop moved to the entry price

complexity.reason: reads position-state (entry price and open profit)

notes: Can occur within a bar or two of entry, or 20+ bars later, per the glossary; no fixed window is implied.

chapter_summary: Front matter: the full List of Terms glossary (pages 13-27) and the 34-page Introduction (pages 31-64). The glossary yielded many primitives Brooks defines once and uses throughout the trilogy (trend bar, doji, inside/outside bar, ii/iii/oio, barbwire, ledge, gap variants, moving-average gap bars, pullback bar, double bottom, shrinking stairs, three pushes) plus the canonical, previously-unstated definition of the High/Low 1-2-3-4 leg-counting setup that T10-23 already relies on. The Introduction contributed a long, repetitive (bull/bear mirrored) checklist of 'signs of strength' in trends, breakouts, and reversals -- mined as a family of context filters and signal-bar quality sub-tests -- plus the standalone 75%-retracement pullback-reclassification rule and a climax/volume-spike pair. Most of the Introduction's remaining bulk (institutional order-flow narrative, news/media, gambling and psychology, the trader's equation) is deliberately non-mechanical and sits in rejected. Primitives here (TrendBar, Doji, InsideBar, OutsideBar) are compact re-definitions of the fuller versions in chapter 7 and chapter 15's SwingHigh/SwingLow, kept minimal only to support this file's own composites; the dedup pass should merge them.
